packages.title: What independent deployments and failures actually show
packages.summary: Two workplace studies, a limited-access chatbot incident, SEC settlements, FINRA guidance, a bounded accounting field study, and a vendor/customer reconciliation story, with measured outcomes and transfer limits kept separate.
packages.scope: Selected independent AI-assistance evidence, accounting field evidence, vendor/customer practice evidence, incidents and governance guidance from 2023–2026. The accounting items are bounded and do not establish end-to-end accounting-agent performance.

questions.question: What changed in the observed customer-support deployment, and whose results differed?
questions.scope: Two original empirical studies reviewed from public NBER/arXiv and HBS/Organization Science materials; evidence concerns workplace AI assistance, not accounting-agent performance.
questions.answer: In a staggered workplace deployment, an AI chat assistant improved customer-support resolution productivity but effects varied sharply by worker skill, and the study did not measure accounting or aggregate employment outcomes.

source_locators.locator: Public author/arXiv version, sections 2.2-2.3, 3.1-3.2, 4 and 5; lines 99-128, 227-251, 254-260 in accessed rendering.

observed_outcomes: 3 million chats associated with 5,179 agents; 1.2 million post-AI chats associated with 1,636 agents
13.8% increase in successfully resolved chats per hour in the author version; published QJE abstract reports 15% for 5,172 agents, so edition-specific figures must be preserved
benefits concentrated among less-skilled/less-experienced agents; treated agents with two months tenure performed comparably to untreated agents with over six months tenure
customer sentiment improved by 0.18 points, about half a standard deviation, while agent sentiment rose only 0.02 points
AI suggestions were optional and absent in a large minority of low-training-data cases
questions.evidence_type: field deployment with staggered rollout and observational/event-study analysis; seven-week 50-agent randomized pilot included but not separately analyzed because small
remaining_gaps: Staggered rollout supports a deployment association under the study design, but transfer to accounting requires separate task and control evaluation; customer support metrics are not financial-statement correctness.

The highest-skilled/most-experienced workers had few positive effects; authors state the setting has a stable product/question environment and results may not generalize to rapidly changing products. The paper does not estimate aggregate employment, wages, long-run skill demand or accounting accuracy.

assessment.basis: Study design, measured population and contrary findings retained; no transfer to accounting-agent reliability is established.

questions.question: When did AI assistance reduce correctness in the consultant experiment?
questions.scope: Two original empirical studies reviewed from public NBER/arXiv and HBS/Organization Science materials; evidence concerns workplace AI assistance, not accounting-agent performance.
questions.answer: A randomized field experiment with expert consultants found strong gains on tasks selected inside GPT-4 capability boundaries but materially worse correctness on one outside-frontier task, demonstrating task-level heterogeneity and overreliance risk.

source_locators.locator: Organization Science published PDF, pp. 2-5 and 8, 11-16; Table 5 p. 8, outside-frontier results p. 11 and summary/boundary conditions pp. 16-17.

observed_outcomes: 758 BCG consultants; 385 inside-frontier and 373 outside-frontier tasks; participants were randomly assigned after a baseline
For 18 inside-frontier tasks, AI groups completed 12.2% more tasks and 25.1% faster on average; the published summary reports quality improvement above 40%/more than 30% depending metric
On the outside-frontier task, controls were correct about 84.5%; GPT-only and GPT+overview groups were correct about 60.0% and 70.6%, averaging a 19 percentage-point decrease
Outside-frontier human graders were blind to condition; GPT-4 grading agreed with human grading in more than 97% of cases
The authors report benefits were largest for bottom-half-skill subjects inside the frontier, while quality could decline outside it
questions.evidence_type: preregistered randomized controlled laboratory-in-the-field experiment; GPT-4, control, and GPT-4 plus overview arms
remaining_gaps: Random assignment supports causal treatment effects for these GPT-4 tasks and BCG population. It does not establish performance for accounting tasks, later models, production controls, incentives, or real filing decisions; the paper itself says tasks approximate but do not fully capture on-the-job complexity.

AI assistance harmed correctness on the outside-frontier task even though participants were highly skilled and did not need to use the AI output; the authors describe overreliance and task-boundary uncertainty. Only one outside-frontier task limits breadth of the negative finding.

assessment.basis: Study design, measured population and contrary findings retained; no transfer to accounting-agent reliability is established.

questions.question: What does the Air Canada chatbot incident establish within the available access limits?
questions.scope: Independent deployment, incident and contrary evidence for accounting-agent governance; benchmark evidence and vendor claims excluded.
questions.answer: A deployed customer-facing chatbot can generate a concrete refund obligation when its inaccurate policy guidance causes reliance; the Air Canada tribunal record is a contrary case to treating the model as an accountability boundary.

source_locators.locator: 2024 BCCRT 149, paras. 1-6 and 19; indexed decision excerpts

remaining_gaps: Single Canadian small-claims tribunal decision; official page was not directly readable in this run; no accounting-agent or journal-posting evidence; cannot estimate frequency or causal risk across deployments.

assessment.basis: Study design, measured population and contrary findings retained; no transfer to accounting-agent reliability is established.

questions.question: What do the SEC AI-marketing settlements show about claims of deployed capability?
questions.scope: Independent deployment, incident and contrary evidence for accounting-agent governance; benchmark evidence and vendor claims excluded.
questions.answer: Independent enforcement found that AI capability claims themselves can be false even when marketed as part of financial services; vendor or issuer claims of AI use should be treated as claims requiring evidence, not deployment proof.
remaining_gaps: The cases concern marketing and disclosure, not accounting-agent transaction execution; settled orders are not a measured benchmark of model accuracy or financial statement impact.

assessment.basis: Study design, measured population and contrary findings retained; no transfer to accounting-agent reliability is established.

questions.question: What does FINRA say about GenAI supervision, and why is that not an empirical result?
questions.scope: Independent deployment, incident and contrary evidence for accounting-agent governance; benchmark evidence and vendor claims excluded.
questions.answer: FINRA’s 2024 notice treats GenAI use as subject to existing supervisory and securities obligations, including when a third-party tool is used, and calls out reliability, accuracy, privacy/integrity, model risk and pre-deployment evaluation.
remaining_gaps: This is regulatory guidance and not an empirical incident study; it reports risk areas and obligations, not measured accounting-agent outcomes or causal effectiveness of controls.

assessment.basis: Study design, measured population and contrary findings retained; no transfer to accounting-agent reliability is established.

questions.question: What does the directly relevant accounting field study establish, and what remains unavailable?
questions.scope: Public Wiley abstract for a Journal of Accounting Research field study involving professional accountants and an AI-enabled accounting platform serving SMEs; accounting-relevant but proprietary and abstract-level.
questions.answer: The abstract reports a survey of 277 professional accountants and proprietary field data from an AI-enabled accounting platform serving 79 SMEs and more than 200,000 transaction-level records. It reports productivity gains, more granular ledgers and faster close, selective intervention when confidence was low, and a risk of error when recommendations were not consensus. The abstract does not expose the full comparator, raw records, journal-population denominator, correction or void behavior, control effectiveness, rights for reuse, or independent replication, so it is relevant field evidence within its stated setting and not a public end-to-end accounting-agent certification.

source_locators.locator: Wiley abstract: 277 professional accountants, AI-enabled platform serving 79 SMEs, more than 200,000 transaction-level records, productivity/reporting-quality outcomes, confidence-dependent intervention and non-consensus recommendation error risk

observed_outcomes: Proprietary platform field data from 79 SMEs and more than 200,000 transaction-level records
Reported productivity gains, more granular ledgers, and faster close
Accountants selectively intervened when confidence was low
Non-consensus AI recommendations could increase error risk

questions.question: How should a vendor/customer reconciliation story be used without turning reported savings into accuracy evidence?
questions.scope: Microsoft customer story for U.S. Venture and US AutoForce using Copilot for Finance; vendor/customer practice evidence, not independent validation.
questions.answer: The customer story reports Dynamics 365 plus Copilot for Finance use in recurring credit-card and bank-statement reconciliations, a four-week setup, and more than 30 hours per month of reported savings, alongside an 80% customer quote. Those statements are useful as a practice example and implementation lead, but the checked story does not publish an independent comparator, error denominator, source-population control, correction register, or reviewer-effectiveness measure. It should not be labeled independent accounting-agent evidence.

observed_outcomes: Recurring credit-card and bank-statement reconciliation use is described
More than 30 hours per month of reported savings and an 80% customer quote are presented by the vendor/customer story
questions.intervention: Dynamics 365 and Copilot for Finance reconciliation workflow
questions.population: U.S. Venture and US AutoForce processes as described by the customer story
questions.comparator: Manual reconciliation baseline is implied by the story but not independently measured or published
questions.outcomes: Reported time savings; no published accuracy, completeness, correction, or control-effectiveness denominator
questions.funding_or_author_relationship: Vendor-published customer story with customer attribution; relationship limits are material to interpretation.
remaining_gaps: No independent accuracy or completeness check was established.
No full population, exception rate, correction history, or reviewer override data was published.
Reported savings are not a causal estimate transferable to the synthetic ERP fixture.

assessment.basis: The source is retained as a clearly labeled practice example with vendor/customer attribution and no independent performance claim.

questions.question: Does the reviewed public evidence establish an independent end-to-end accounting-agent deployment?
questions.scope: Comparison across the accounting field study, vendor/customer story, general workplace experiments, federal governance evidence, and the synthetic ERP fixture.
questions.answer: No. The accounting field study is directly relevant but abstract-level and proprietary; the customer story is vendor/customer reported; general workplace experiments do not measure ledger correctness; GAO and NIST materials concern governance or evaluation framing; and the ERP fixture is original synthetic data. The evidence gap is itself a required assessment result: a deployment claim needs an accounting task denominator, source-population and correction controls, comparator, reviewer actions, incidents, costs, rights, and independent verification before it can support transfer.

source_locators.locator: Wiley abstract and stated proprietary field setting
Microsoft vendor/customer story and reported reconciliation savings
GAO-26-107522 IRS AI governance and information-quality findings, not accounting accuracy

remaining_gaps: No public independent end-to-end accounting-agent deployment with ledger correctness and control evidence was established.
No independent replication of the field study or validation of the vendor/customer story was established.
No live ERP run, reviewer study, incident register, or rights-cleared deployment dataset was obtained.

assessment.basis: The selected sources support a bounded accounting field study and a vendor/customer practice example, but the requested end-to-end deployment evidence remains absent.

workflows: Pin the study edition and measured population before comparing outcomes.
Retain the task denominator, baseline, contrary result, access scope and causal limits.
For accounting use, request separate ledger correctness, error correction, population completeness, cost and human-review evidence.
Classify the Human + AI in Accounting abstract as directly relevant but proprietary field evidence, and classify the U.S. Venture story as vendor/customer practice evidence.
Do not convert general workplace experiments, NIST/GAO governance evidence, benchmarks, or synthetic fixtures into an accounting deployment claim.
coverage_gaps: No independent end-to-end accounting-agent deployment is established by this packet.
The accounting field study is available at abstract level with proprietary methods and records.
The U.S. Venture item is vendor/customer reported and lacks an independent accuracy denominator.
